Real wasabi is a fresh, delicate plant with a complex, herbaceous flavor and a sharp heat that quickly fades, while "fake" wasabi is typically a cheaper imitation made from horseradish, mustard, and green food coloring that has a harsher, more pungent, and longer-lasting kick. Real wasabi is expensive and perishable, so it is freshly grated just before serving, while fake wasabi has a neon-green color and a smooth, often gritty texture from its ingredients.

A massively underrated restaurant in Palisades Park. 

📍East Seafood Restaurant aka Dong Hae Seafood
Palisades Park

- hwedupbap (fresh sashimi over vegetables and rice) - lunch combo comes with udon and tempura
- grilled mackerel and soybean paste stew combo

Why is it so good?
- the quality of the fish is so good; everything was prepared perfectly 
- there’s a parking lot with FREE parking 🙌
- other diners conversation with the server showed they were returning customers 
- they offer the lunch prices on all SEVEN days of the week from 11:30 - 3pm
- all of this food came out to $55 before tip 🥹

Excuse me as I run back there. 🏃
Wishing our members and the whole Palisades Park community a restful break and a very happy holiday! ❄️ #ppea #ppeaproud #palparkea #palisadespark

The Band:

Annie Chen is a remarkable vocalist, composer, and bandleader originally from Beijing, who has called New York home since 2013. Currently, Annie is leading her ensemble, Guardians, which released its self-titled debut album on February 23, 2024, through JZ Music. The album has garnered significant acclaim, described as “stunning” by Women in Jazz Media, and praised by Jazz in Europe for its “clear vision and message.” Peter Quinn of Jazzwise commended the music’s “striking sonorities, compelling narrative, and Chen’s remarkably expressive voice,” emphasizing that it’s an album worth revisiting to uncover its intricate details. In 2024, Guardians made it to the first round of Grammy nominations for Best Alternative Jazz Album.

Matei Predescu is a gifted Romanian-American pianist, keyboardist, composer, and improviser known for his eclectic musical pursuits. As a composer, Predescu skillfully balances musical density with open space, while his improvisational approach draws from the innovative styles of jazz legends like McCoy Tyner, Cecil Taylor, Geri Allen, and Fred Hersch, all the while remaining rooted in the blues traditions of Thelonious Monk.

Max Bessesen is a versatile multi-woodwind instrumentalist and composer based in Brooklyn. Recognized for his “saxophone virtuosity” by Downbeat, he has performed with bands led by renowned artists such as Miguel Zenon, Mimi Jones, and Darcy James Argue. His 2020 album, Trouble (Ropeadope), features the talented Ron Miles, and the single “Bakkam” earned him an ASCAP Young Jazz Composer Award.

BILLY BUDD
(clarified)
From our menu chapter: Nightfall 

Base Spirit: White Rum, Falernum 
Citrus: Lime, Grapefruit 
Spices: Ginger, Allspice, Clove, Cinnamon 
Nuts: Almonds 

This cocktail has made sporadic appearances on our menu over the years and remains a beloved choice. Its simplicity, featuring just few ingredients, allows the rum to take center stage. We utilize the delicious Ten to One white rum, known for its vibrant grassy notes accompanied by subtle hints of pineapple, banana, jasmine, and a touch of white pepper. 

The drink draws inspiration from Herman Melville’s novella, which delves into the battle between good and evil, the tension between law and morality, and the theme of lost innocence. The character of Billy Budd, depicted as a young, pure, and striking figure, is likened to Adam in a pre-Fall state...

💢We are delighted to share the news of our new Head Bartender: Yordi Coyotecalt!

Yordi originally from Mexico, moved to the United States as a teenager. With a rich background in bartending, he has refined his craft at some of New York’s finest establishments, including Lilli’s Victorian Establishment, Ophelia Lounge, The Dominick Hotel, and The Rum House, among others. Now, he’s eager to bring his expertise to Sugar Monk, where he will continue to showcase his skills in the art of mixology.

As our fourth Head Bartender in over six and a half years of Sugar Monk’s life, Yordi also makes history as our first Latino & Mexican Mestizo (of Aztec and Spanish heritage) Head Bartender! 

We are incredibly excited to have him at the forefront as we embrace a new era of innovative techniques and concepts, while increasingly featuring our own spirits created at our Brooklyn distillery, @atherasspirits.

Cheers to new adventures!

This is Harlem!
This is Harlem, and these are the places that best represent it today. It is the people and families who live and work in it that make it special: every day they continue, without stopping, to express themselves with authenticity, creativity and a strength that no one can stop. Harlem is unique, and every time I visit these places I feel that spark that makes me say: “There! This is really living”. And maybe, if you happen around here, we’ll cross paths on Lenox avenue, we’ll exchange a smile and for a moment we’ll be part of the same rhythm. That day, remember to add some pride to your day and say with your heart: “Hey! Today I’m in Harlem, baby!”

Headed into the Cotton Club to listen to some jazz music. 🎷🎷Jazz music is giving African Americans the voice they have always wanted. It is really helping create a new cultural identity for us African Americans. Today, a black artist is performing for a mostly white crowd.

To celebrate International Jazz Day with the @dreambuilderslug, allow me to present another Baltimore jazz legend:

Cabell “Cab” Calloway III
“The Hi De Ho Man” 🎙️

A man of many firsts was born on Christmas Day in 1907. Known for his energetic performances that mixed jazz and vaudeville, Calloway began performing in Baltimore night clubs after high school and later relocated to New York where he and his orchestra became a household name at the Cotton Club in Harlem. 

As a heavy influencer of popular culture, Cab was the first African American to record a single that sold a million copies, “Minnie the Moocher”. He was also the first African American to have a nationally syndicated radio show. He produced A “Hepster’s” Dictionary, the first dictionary published by an African American introducing the world to the language of jive. 

From Betty Boop to zoot suits, Cab charmed the world with his scat-jive vocals and influenced some of our biggest entertainers to date.  He is one of the greatest entertainers of the Big Band/Swing era.

Actress, singer, dancer & Civil Rights activist Lena Horne — with beloved pug, Nellie (a gift from second husband, Lennie Hayton) and then with her pick of the litter, Pekinese pup named Champagne (second from the right).

BedStuy-born Lena Mary Calhoun Horne (June 30, 1917 – May 9, 2010) joined the chorus of the Cotton Club at the age of sixteen and became a nightclub performer before moving on to Hollywood and Broadway.

A groundbreaking African-American performer, Horne advocated for civil rights and took part in the March on Washington in August 1963. Horne was at an NAACP rally with Medgar Evers in Jackson, Mississippi, the weekend before Evers was assassinated. At the March on Washington she spoke and performed on behalf of the NAACP, S.N.C.C., and the National Council of Negro Women. She also worked with Eleanor Roosevelt in attempts to pass anti-lynching laws.

Exceptional Dining Experience at AP Rooftop

We had an absolutely unforgettable dinner at AP Rooftop. Two of us had been before and couldn’t wait to bring friends and it exceeded expectations yet again.

The restaurant was filled to capacity, yet the atmosphere was perfectly balanced, lively and vibrant without being overwhelming. The music blended seamlessly with the energy of the room, and we could still hold a conversation without ever needing to raise our voices a rare and welcome touch in a bustling, popular spot.

We started with cocktails that set the tone for the evening: a dirty martini that was impossibly smooth, a white Burgundy that was light, crisp, and elegant, and a gimlet mixed to absolute perfection.

Our appetizers the whipped brie and piccata calamari were divine. The brie was luxuriously creamy with just the right balance of sweet and savory, and the calamari was tender with a bright, flavorful sauce that made every bite sing.

For entrées, we shared the lamb chops, bucatini & clams, and short rib ragout each dish somehow better than the last. The lamb was beautifully cooked and bursting with flavor, the pasta perfectly al dente, and the ragout rich and comforting without being heavy.

And then came dessert the pumpkin cheesecake. Now, I’m not a pumpkin person, but this was otherworldly. Light, airy, and almost cloud-like more like eating a pumpkin-spiced dream than a traditional cheesecake.

We asked to meet Executive Chef Rob, who graciously came to our table. His passion and talent shine through in every dish, and it was such a pleasure to thank him personally.

A special thank you to our server Lauren, whose warmth, attentiveness, and perfect pacing made the evening effortless from start to finish.

AP Rooftop is that rare combination of exceptional food, flawless cocktails, and genuine hospitality, all wrapped in an atmosphere that’s both energetic and comfortable. A true gem we’ll absolutely go back again and again.

It’s not just about choosing between lunch options or what to wear. Sometimes decision paralysis runs deep👇🏻

It can be tied to the fear of upsetting others, feeling responsible for their moods, or not being “perfect” enough.

When you grow up trying to manage everyone else’s feelings, it’s easy to lose sight of your own. 

The need to keep the peace, avoid conflict, and make everyone happy becomes deeply ingrained. 

And now, as an adult, you’re facing decisions that force you to prioritize your own needs and it can feel extremely paralyzing and frustrating.

So, why does decision paralysis happen? When you’ve been conditioned to keep everyone else happy, the idea of disappointing someone feels like a huge risk. 

You might fear rejection, conflict, or the idea that you’re being selfish by choosing your own needs.

 It’s a heavy burden to carry, and it leaves you stuck, overthinking, and second-guessing every choice you make.

But what if we flipped the script? What if choosing what’s right for you didn’t have to come with guilt?

Remind yourself:

✨You are allowed to make decisions that prioritize your own needs, even if it means disappointing someone else. It doesn’t make you a bad person or selfish—it makes you human. When you start respecting your own feelings, you teach others to do the same.

✨You can’t control how others feel, but you can control how you respond to your own needs. Every time you make a decision that puts you first, you’re practicing self-respect and growth.

If this resonates with you, share it with someone who needs to hear this reminder today 🫶🏻

From general surgery → hand surgery → the brachial plexus capital of the world 

I didn’t start out planning to become a peripheral nerve surgeon. 

I began my training in general surgery, drawn to the challenge of limb replants. That interest led me into hand surgery, where during fellowship I was assigned a topic nobody wanted — neuromas and neurolysis. 

At the time, it almost felt like a punishment, but it CHANGED the course of my life. 

I was hooked!

A few months later, I had a defining moment when guest lecturer, Dr. Raja Sabapathy, gave a week long grand round series on replants, brachial plexus injuries, and complex upper extremity reconstruction. 

I told him I wanted to go to Coimbatore, India and be one of his fellows at the Ganga Hospital, one of the HIGHEST VOLUME brachial plexus centers in the world — performing 450 brachial plexus surgeries per year! 

Training there, learning from the masters in the field, fundamentally shaped how I think about nerve surgery. 

Today, my practice focuses on peripheral nerve surgery, brachial plexus reconstruction, and advanced nerve techniques designed to restore movement, reduce pain, and improve quality of life. 

Sometimes the path finds you before you even realize you’re looking for it!
